question: A student wants to find out how much time residents across a city spend reading each day. The student randomly stops 100 readers at a library entrance to survey them. The main problem with this survey is
solution: Sampling only people at a library entrance excludes many residents and does not give a representative sample of the city. People in this sample may read more, so the survey may overestimate average reading time; an overestimate is not guaranteed.
